title: Slot Exchange Scheduler — probe notes and tuning hypotheses
content:
Summary:

This is a working log from an experiment series exploring a "slot-exchange" scheduling primitive for the continuous batcher. The primitive lets priority/BW classes temporarily swap queue slots to reduce long-tail latency for urgent requests while preserving overall throughput. The goal is to find knobs that reduce P99 without regressing P50 or throughput, and to capture microtrace signatures that indicate slot contention vs kernel-induced stalls.

Why this is different: many previous notes focus on timeouts, coalescing windows and urgency weights. Slot-exchange is a lightweight cooperative reallocation at enqueue time + opportunistic swap at flush time. It's a middle ground between hard preemption and simple priority demotion.

Hypotheses:
- H1: Opportunistic slot exchanges reduce P99 by allowing small urgent requests to use an otherwise underfilled batch that would have waited until timeout.
- H2: Aggressive exchange thresholds (low exchange_threshold_ms) will increase batch churn and harm throughput by increasing small-batch kernel overhead.
- H3: Adding a decay window for exchange frequency (fairness_decay_ms) prevents starvation in best-effort classes while still improving tails for high-priority traffic.

Experiment setup (cluster):
- 4x serving nodes, A100-80GB, 64GB host RAM, 32 vCPU each
- Model: rl-llama-7b-quant (single-GPU per worker runtime)
- Batching runtime: continuous-batcher v2.9 (branch: slot-exchange-probe)
- Workloads: mixed (50% low-priority long-gen 512 tokens, 30% medium 128 tokens, 20% high-priority short 16 tokens). Arrival process: Poisson with bursts emulated by gamma interarrival scaling.
- Baseline config: max_batch_size=64, timeout_ms=12, slot_holding_time_ms=1000, no exchanges.
- Probe configs: exchange_enabled=true/false, exchange_threshold_ms={2,6,12}, fairness_decay_ms={50,200,1000}, max_exchanges_per_window={1,4,inf}.
- Each test run: 30 minutes steady-state, repeated 3 times per config, synthetic trace replays for determinism. Metrics collected: latency P50/P95/P99, throughput (req/s), tokens/s, GPU occupancy, kernel invocation counts, cpu-side scheduling counters, batch size distribution histogram, exchange_count/time series.

Representative results (median across runs) — baseline vs tuned probe:
- Baseline (no exchange): P50=48ms, P95=210ms, P99=940ms, throughput=820 req/s, avg_batch_size=27
- Probe A (exchange_threshold_ms=6, fairness_decay_ms=200, max_exchanges=1): P50=50ms, P95=195ms, P99=610ms, throughput=780 req/s, avg_batch_size=25, exchange_rate=32 exchanges/s
- Probe B (exchange_threshold_ms=2, fairness_decay_ms=50, max_exchanges=4): P50=57ms, P95=240ms, P99=520ms, throughput=690 req/s, avg_batch_size=19, exchange_rate=86 exchanges/s
- Probe C (aggressive exchange, no decay): P50=62ms, P95=280ms, P99=480ms, throughput=610 req/s, avg_batch_size=16, exchange_rate=120 exchanges/s

Quick interpretation:
- Exchange reduces P99 substantially (baseline 940 -> 480–610ms depending on aggressiveness) at the cost of throughput and P50 increases. This matches H1 and H2.
- There is a clear tradeoff curve: lower exchange_threshold_ms allows urgent requests to join earlier but increases small-batch overhead.
- Fairness decay helps avoid complete starvation of lower tiers; decay_ms around 200ms seems a reasonable middle ground in our workload.

Microtrace inspection (examples):
- Before: long tail traces show a burst where a medium-priority request waited nearly 10x its generation time inside the queue due to a sequence of large low-priority arrivals that consumed batch formation windows. CPU callstack shows continuous batching loop in sleep then wake, then kernel launch with large batch creation overhead.
- After (Probe A): a P99 trace starts with a high-priority request held 6ms in primary queue but then exchanged into a half-filled batch at flush time; kernel latency unchanged but end-to-end reduced by 420ms.
- After (Probe C): we observed kernel churn: many tiny batches caused GPU kernel overhead (kernel-launch tail) — GPU occupancy dropped intermittently.

Profiling notes (where bottlenecks seemed to originate):
- Queue-time vs kernel-time split: with exchanges enabled, queue-time drops for high-priority requests but kernel-time contribution to tail rises due to many small kernels. The two are anti-correlated as exchange aggressiveness increases.
- CPU scheduling: exchange path adds a lock hop (slot ownership swap). Under high exchange_rate this caused measurable contention on the batcher mutex (seen in perf flamegraphs).
- Memory pressure: none significant in these runs; KV-cache unaffected.
- Kernel hotspots: repeated small launches show increased per-launch overhead (warmup amortized inefficiently).

Operational knobs to surface in Console (proposed):
- exchange_enabled (bool)
- exchange_threshold_ms (int)
- fairness_decay_ms (int)
- max_exchanges_per_window (int)
- exchange_priority_floor (enum: none/low/medium) — prevents exchange if donor slot priority < floor
- exchange_telemetry (bool) — emit exchange_count and post-exchange batch_size histogram

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Q1: How does slot-exchange interact with KV-cache prefill patterns? Need a test where resumed sequences rely on large KV caches; small batches might miss prefill benefits.
- Q2: What are long-term GPU efficiency/price impacts at scale? Small-batch kernel churn could meaningfully increase unit cost; need cost-modeled run at 100-node scale.
- Q3: Is there a deterministic, low-lock alternative to implement exchange (lock-free slot handoff)? Prototype idea: per-queue handoff queue with atomic CAS on slot descriptors. Microbench this.
- Q4: Do we need a hybrid policy that limits exchange during high-AI-cost kernels (long-generations) but allows during short-text workloads? (workload-aware thresholds)

Action items (next steps):
- [Arjun] implement exchange_telemetry for detailed per-batch annotations (due 2024-12-01)
- [Sofia] run cost-sensitivity sweep on 50-node replay cluster using representative customer traces (due 2024-12-15)
- [Maya] prototype lock-free handoff sketch and microbenchmark in user-space (due 2024-12-22)
- Add a small PR to Console to surface exchange toggles behind feature flag (owner: eng-console)

Decision log (tentative):
- We will merge exchange_enabled behind a runtime feature flag into next canary but default it OFF for hosted customers.
- For Dedicated customers and internal perf teams, enable probe default on non-prod clusters for further telemetry.

Notes to self (raw observations / loose thoughts):
- Exchange_threshold ~= half of timeout seems to capture useful early joins without too much churn in these traces. Eg: timeout=12ms, threshold=6ms performed well.
- Tradeoff surface looks like a convex curve; need automated tuning (Optimize) to pick per-customer operating point based on cost vs tail-SLO.
- Consider a combined signal for exchange: not just queue waiting time but also donor batch fullness and donor-request-cost-estimate (if available) to avoid stealing from batches that would otherwise amortize kernel cost (long gen donors).

References / links:
- Related experiment: JIRA-RT-1310 (mini-slot-affinity work) — some conceptual overlap but different implementation
- Design doc draft: confluence.redwood/slot-exchange-design-v1
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2193 (slot-exchange PoC)

End of note.

(If you want raw CSV exports of the runs, ping me; I kept the full traces and perf profiles in /mnt/exp/slot-exchange/.)
